final_proof:
**Remark on the statement.** The statement calls $f \wedge g$ the "pointwise maximum", but defines it by $(f\wedge g)(s)=\min\{f(s),g(s)\}$. This is just a wrong word; the formula and the claim are about the pointwise minimum, and that is what we prove.

**Claim.** For all $s \in S$: $(f \wedge g)(s) = \tfrac12\big(f(s)+g(s)-|f(s)-g(s)|\big)$. So $f \wedge g = \tfrac12\,(f+g-|f-g|)$ as mappings $S \to \mathbb{R}$.

**Proof.** Both sides are mappings from $S$ to $\mathbb{R}$. Two mappings with the same domain and codomain are equal exactly when they agree at every point. So we only need to check the values at each point.

By definition of the pointwise operations, for every $s \in S$:
- $(f+g)(s) = f(s)+g(s)$,
- $(f-g)(s) = f(s)-g(s)$,
- $|f-g|(s) = |(f-g)(s)| = |f(s)-g(s)|$,
- $(f+g-|f-g|)(s) = f(s)+g(s)-|f(s)-g(s)|$,
- $\big(\tfrac12(f+g-|f-g|)\big)(s) = \tfrac12\big(f(s)+g(s)-|f(s)-g(s)|\big)$.

Fix $s \in S$ and write $a = f(s)$ and $b = g(s)$, both real numbers. We must show
$$\min\{a,b\} = \tfrac12\big(a+b-|a-b|\big).$$
Because $\mathbb{R}$ is totally ordered, either $a \le b$ or $b < a$.

*Case 1: $a \le b$.* Then $\min\{a,b\} = a$. Also $a-b \le 0$, so $|a-b| = -(a-b) = b-a$. Hence
$$\tfrac12\big(a+b-|a-b|\big) = \tfrac12\big(a+b-(b-a)\big) = \tfrac12(2a) = a = \min\{a,b\}.$$

*Case 2: $b < a$.* Then $\min\{a,b\} = b$. Also $a-b > 0$, so $|a-b| = a-b$. Hence
$$\tfrac12\big(a+b-|a-b|\big) = \tfrac12\big(a+b-(a-b)\big) = \tfrac12(2b) = b = \min\{a,b\}.$$

The two cases cover every possibility, so the identity holds for all real $a,b$. In particular it holds for $a=f(s)$ and $b=g(s)$. This gives
$$(f\wedge g)(s) = \min\{f(s),g(s)\} = \tfrac12\big(f(s)+g(s)-|f(s)-g(s)|\big) = \big(\tfrac12(f+g-|f-g|)\big)(s).$$
Since $s \in S$ was arbitrary, the two mappings agree at every point of $S$. Therefore $f \wedge g = \tfrac12\,(f+g-|f-g|)$. $\blacksquare$

(If $S=\varnothing$, both sides are the empty mapping, so the equality holds trivially. The argument above covers this case too, since there is no point to check.)
